report.interpretation: Total claim payments with a payment date from 2026-01-01 to the extract date, 2026-09-30. I read "this year" as calendar 2026 and counted by payment date, which is the agreed paid_amount definition. I excluded 159 duplicate rows from the 'reload-2026-03-14' batch, which the data-quality check flagged.
report.answer: We have paid about $29.99M on claims so far in 2026 (1 Jan to 30 Sep). The raw payment table shows $30.89M. That figure includes $0.89M of duplicate rows from a March re-load, which I removed.
report.answer_sql: SELECT sum(amount) AS paid_ytd_usd FROM claim_payments WHERE payment_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-09-30' AND load_batch NOT LIKE 'reload-%'

findings.claim: YTD 2026 payments are $29.99M after removing the duplicated reload batch. All 159 reload rows exactly match payments already loaded in nightly batches.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT sum(amount) AS raw_total, sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE load_batch NOT LIKE 'reload-%') AS dedup_total, sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE load_batch LIKE 'reload-%') AS reload_total FROM claim_payments WHERE payment_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-09-30'

data_quality_issues.issue: The batch reload-2026-03-14 loaded 159 payment rows a second time (payments dated 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13).
data_quality_issues.impact: The raw sum overstates paid by $892,999. The standard paid_amount metric would include this unless the rows are excluded.

proposed_actions.title: Remove duplicate payments from reload-2026-03-14
proposed_actions.reason: 159 rows duplicate nightly-loaded payments and inflate paid totals by about $893K.
